statement: A proper birational replacement does not in general preserve codimension at least two for the full inverse image of an omitted set. One sufficient extra condition is quasi-finiteness over that set: for integral n-dimensional varieties Y and X over a field, a finite-type map f:Y→X quasi-finite over Z⊂X with dim Z≤n−2 has dim f⁻¹(Z)≤n−2.
hypotheses: The positive repair explicitly assumes equal-dimensional integral varieties, a closed subset Z, and quasi-finiteness over Z; the original unrestricted proper birational reduction does not have this condition.
proof_or_counterexample: Bl_0(A²)→A² has exceptional inverse image P¹ of the codimension-two origin. In the chart y=xt the inverse image is x=0, a divisor. For the repaired case every irreducible component of f⁻¹(Z) is quasi-finite over its image, so its dimension is at most dim Z.
scope: Refutes the codimension-preservation inference only. It does not refute surrounding finite-generation or purity theorems, and it does not assert that an arbitrary Chow modification has the new quasi-finiteness property.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: Let f:X→P^r_k be a finite-type morphism with X geometrically irreducible and n=dim closure(f(X)). For 1≤s≤n−1, the inverse image of the generic codimension-s linear subspace is geometrically irreducible over the parameter field. Ordinary irreducibility over k does not suffice for that geometric conclusion.
hypotheses: Geometric irreducibility, finite type, and the stated image-dimension range. Neither properness nor normality is added to this generic irreducibility assertion.
proof_or_counterexample: P²_C viewed over R is integral but splits into two copies after base change to C; its geometric generic section is reducible. The later scan113 adds geometric irreducibility. Poonen–Slavov1.8 with Lemma7.1 and§7 gives the corrected general-morphism hyperplane form; iterating generic sections gives the stated codimension range.
scope: This repairs the generic geometric-irreducibility statement, not the distinct π₁ theorem CL023. The later π₁ corollaries still require their separate global hypotheses and are refuted in the pinching example under weaker local assumptions.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: Connectedness of X alone does not ensure connectedness of a generic positive-dimensional linear section. The geometric-irreducibility hypothesis in REF-CL-SA12-021 is a sufficient replacement in its stated dimension range.
hypotheses: Counterexample over C: the union of two projective planes in P⁴ meeting at a single point; f is the closed inclusion and s=1.
proof_or_counterexample: The union is connected and reduced. A hyperplane missing the intersection point cuts two disjoint projective lines, so the generic section is disconnected. The source itself rejects the connectedness replacement.
scope: This is the precise rejected weakening of generic Bertini. It does not substitute the unrelated fundamental-group theorem as the repaired statement.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: The regular locus of an arbitrary proper normal model need not have the birational fundamental group. If the fixed function field admits a proper regular model Z, the inverse system over proper normal models is essentially constant on a cofinal family dominating Z, with group π₁(Z); this does not identify π₁(X_reg) for every other normal model X.
hypotheses: The positive comparison assumes a fixed proper regular model. The negative example is over C, where the rational function field has regular proper model P².
proof_or_counterexample: For X=(P¹×P¹)/((x,y)↦(−x,−y)), the regular locus has a connected étale double cover. In invariant coordinates a=x²,t=y/x, its extension adjoins √a and ramifies at the a-adic valuation, which has a centre on every proper model. Such a cover cannot be étale on any proper modification. Purity and normal graph closures give the corrected regular-model comparison.
scope: The failure is geometric and survives every proper modification. It is not merely an abstract warning about inverse systems; uniform finite generation alone is also insufficient for stabilization, but that is a different point.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: For a regular integral noetherian scheme Y and an open U whose complement has codimension at least two, restriction Pic(Y)→Pic(U) is an isomorphism. Replacing Y by a proper birational source X in that display is false in general.
hypotheses: Regular integral noetherian Y; codimension measured in Y. This is a statement about line-bundle classes. It does not certify the separate nonreduced Picard-scheme birational theorem.
proof_or_counterexample: Regularity gives local factoriality, so Weil/Cartier divisors and their rational-function relations extend across a codimension-two omission. If X=Bl_p(P²) and U=P²∖{p}, the nontrivial exceptional line bundle O_X(E) restricts trivially on the inverse copy of U; its degree−1 on E proves nontriviality.
scope: The mathematically correct target letter is Y in this repair. Both text witnesses display X, so the archival reading remains unresolved rather than silently changed.
evidence: Pro raw936–959 reread in closing audit
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: A closed inclusion of group schemes is not determined by its geometric points and tangent spaces. For finite k-group schemes, the stronger condition that a closed inclusion H→G have equal scheme lengths does force an isomorphism.
hypotheses: The positive criterion is restricted to finite group schemes over a field. It is not claimed as a proof of the broader Picard-scheme assertion.
proof_or_counterexample: In characteristic p, α_p⊂α_{p²} has one geometric point on each side and an isomorphism on one-dimensional tangent spaces, but lengths p and p². For the repaired finite criterion, the coordinate-ring map is a surjection of finite-dimensional k-vector spaces of equal dimensions, hence an isomorphism.
scope: Refutes the bare points-plus-tangents inference. Additional infinitesimal control is needed in the original geometry; no counterexample to CL033 itself is supplied.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: Bounds on dimension, geometric-point torsion and tangent dimension do not force stabilization of finite group schemes under closed inclusions. A uniform bound on their actual scheme lengths does force eventual constancy of such a filtered increasing system.
hypotheses: For the positive criterion all terms are finite group schemes over one field and transition maps are closed immersions; scheme length, not number of geometric points, is uniformly bounded.
proof_or_counterexample: The chain α_{p^m} has dimension0, a single geometric point and tangent dimension1, but length p^m. For the repaired criterion, lengths form a bounded nondecreasing set of integers; choose a term of maximal length. Every later closed immersion has equal length and is an isomorphism by REF-CL-SA12-037.
scope: This refutes the abstract criterion only under the geometric-point interpretation of torsion. If the draft means a uniform bound on entire finite subgroup-scheme orders, the example does not satisfy that hypothesis. No new geometric counterexample to all-model Pic^τ stabilization is asserted.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: For an abelian variety A over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and a prime ℓ≠p, T_ℓ A is free of rank2 dim A. For the proper geometrically normal Picard setting, retain the Kummer identification T_ℓ Pic≅H¹_et(X,Z_ℓ(1)) and its dual/twist relationship with π₁^ab; the characteristic-primary rank does not give2 dim A.
hypotheses: The rank formula is prime to the characteristic and concerns the reduced abelian Picard variety. Characteristic0 permits every prime.
proof_or_counterexample: The nonsingular elliptic curve y²=x³−x in characteristic3 has four F₃-points and trace0; the opened supersingularity criterion gives p-rank0 although its Picard variety has dimension1. The ℓ≠p Tate module has rank2.
scope: Repairs the rank formula itself, not the separate uniform dimension-bound theorem CL049. The Tate twist and dual matter for functorial statements even when ranks agree.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: For a field extension K/k, if Spec(K) is geometrically integral over k, then K⊗_k kbar is a field. Geometric normality alone permits a product of fields and is insufficient; alternatively a geometric component must be chosen explicitly.
hypotheses: kbar is an algebraic closure. Geometric integrality is the added hypothesis; no silent reinterpretation of the historical phrase normal over k is made.
proof_or_counterexample: C⊗_R C≅C×C although Spec(C) is geometrically normal over R. Under geometric integrality the tensor product is a domain and is integral over K because kbar/k is algebraic; an integral domain algebraic over a field is a field.
scope: Repairs the field notation, not the neighboring Picard-dimension claim CL049. Choosing a component changes the base data and must be recorded.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: For a smooth connected curve C over an algebraically closed field of characteristic exponent p, C not a proper genus-zero curve, and a finite constant abelian group A of order prime to p, the filtered colimit of H^q_et(C′,A) over connected finite tame covers C′→C is zero for every q>0. P¹ with empty boundary is an exception: it has no nontrivial connected finite étale cover and H²(P¹,μ_n)≅Z/n for n>1 prime to p.
hypotheses: Finite coefficients, smooth curves and prime-to-characteristic order. Tame covers are measured at the points of a smooth compactification. No unrestricted profinite-coefficient inverse-limit assertion is included.
proof_or_counterexample: A finite-coefficient H¹ class is killed by its torsor. Affine smooth curves have prime-to-p cohomological dimension at most1. For proper genus at least1, H² with cyclic prime-to-p coefficients is killed by a finite étale cover of degree divisible by the coefficient order; such covers exist from the nonzero prime-to-p abelianized fundamental group. Degrees above2 vanish. P¹ instead has the displayed nonzero H² and trivial π₁.
scope: Repairs the all-curves higher-cohomology assertion itself. The earlier event pointed only to the H¹ lemma CL083, which was insufficient as a refined target. This finite-colimit statement does not identify a vague π₂ object or interchange arbitrary inverse limits.
evidence: Milne2008 finite-coefficient curve discussion as previously logged
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: If i:X₀→X is a nilpotent closed immersion, n is invertible on X, and L is a fixed line bundle on X, restriction is an equivalence between the groupoids of pairs (M,φ:M^n≅L) on X and (M₀,φ₀:M₀^n≅i*L) on X₀. This does not imply unique n-divisibility of ker(Pic(X)→Pic(X₀)).
hypotheses: Finite nilpotent thickening, fixed L and specified power isomorphism, n invertible. Infinite formal effectiveness and algebraization require additional conditions.
proof_or_counterexample: Étale nil-invariance identifies the μ_n-gerbes of roots and their obstruction/torsor/automorphism data. The counterexample glues X₀=E×G_m by z_j=z_i(1+εa_ij): the kernel is H¹(X₀,O)/Za and a/n gives nonzero n-torsion. Its special-fibre root pair has nonzero power-isomorphism class z modulo nth powers, so it is not the trivial μ_n-torsor.
scope: This replaces the failed Picard-kernel assertion with the root-pair statement actually needed for fixed-root lifting. It does not assert the kernel is uniquely divisible, nor that every formal system algebraizes.
evidence: root independent audit recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: For a square-zero thickening X₀⊂X with ideal I and n invertible, assume Γ(X,O_X*)→Γ(X₀,O_X₀*) is surjective. Then Pic(X)[n]→Pic(X₀)[n] is bijective. Without control of the global-unit boundary, this unrestricted Pic[n] assertion is false.
hypotheses: Square-zero I, n invertible, and explicit surjectivity on global units. A finite nilpotent tower satisfies the analogous conclusion if this units hypothesis holds at every square-zero stage.
proof_or_counterexample: The units exact sequence and surjectivity make the Picard kernel H¹(X₀,I), on which multiplication by n is bijective. The obstruction to lifting an n-torsion line bundle lies in H²(X₀,I), where n is injective; it therefore vanishes. A lift can be adjusted by the unique nth root of its nth power in the kernel. Injectivity follows because that kernel has no n-torsion. The E×G_m deformation violates the units hypothesis: δ(z)=±a and the resulting quotient has torsion.
scope: This is a precise sufficient repair for the particular opened Stacks0C6S statement. It does not edit the external source or claim that its unrestricted assertion is reliable background. The needed units condition is stronger than an arbitrary nilpotent thickening.
provenance: Modern repair or precise negative conclusion of this review; not an authorial quotation or an ink correction.

statement: Retain the normal-bundle H2 extension class; pi2=0 does not imply a split extension.
Restrict to a category in which the equalizer is finite flat and the required torsor reductions exist; variable-base maps cannot be admitted without this.
Use the punctured complement of the normal-crossing divisor for the rank-two inertia expression; the unpunctured strictly henselian spectrum has trivial pi1.
Require a global geometric-unibranch/normal or connected-cover irreducibility hypothesis for pi1 surjectivity; a small image of the local bad locus is insufficient.
Retain proper geometric connectedness of all sections; the additional pi1 consequence needs a global connected-cover irreducibility hypothesis.
Use a precise normal/regular tame Lefschetz theorem with its global assumptions; the written local-along-section hypotheses fail already with empty boundary.
The finite étale version is valid; the arbitrary nonseparated étale version is false.
Ordinary étale pi1 of the rational nodal curve is full Zhat, including its p-component.
Use uniformly continuous maps to discrete sets, or a finite compact inverse system; ordinary continuity is insufficient.
